findings.title: chemtrails 'past' trail shows ~the whole trajectory (future included) for the first tail_duration seconds, then snaps to empty (matplotlib 3-D AND 2-D; plotly is correct, so the backends diverge)
findings.description: In the matplotlib backend's parallel-animation update callbacks, the chemtrails-only branch slices the past trail as data[0 : num - window_frames + 1] (hypertools/plot/matplotlib_backend.py lines 992-993, and the 2-D twin at lines 1697-1698). For num < window_frames - 1 the stop index is NEGATIVE, so Python slices from the END: at frame 0 of the verbatim chemtrails.py example the 'past' trail contains 842 of the 901 points (nearly the whole trajectory, i.e. the FUTURE), grows to 900 points by frame 58, snaps to 0 at frame 59, and only then regrows correctly. With the default tail_duration=2 / frame_rate=30 this is the first 2 seconds of every chemtrails animation -- including the gallery gif. The plotly backend grows the trail correctly from the start (frame 0: 1 point), so identical calls render differently on the two backends for the first window. precog and bullettime are unaffected (their slices cannot go negative). Verified in 3-D (weights_avg verbatim example) and 2-D (synthetic 100x4). Fix: clamp the stop, e.g. data[0 : max(0, num - window + 1)].
findings.repro:
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
data = hyp.load('weights_avg')
fig, ani = hyp.plot(data, animate=True, chemtrails=True, show=False)
ani._init_draw()
ax = fig.axes[0]
trail = [ln for ln in ax.get_lines() if ln.get_alpha() == 0.3][0]
for f in [0, 30, 58, 59, 60, 120]:
    ani._draw_frame(f)
    print(f, len(trail.get_xdata()))
findings.expected: Past trail length grows 0/1 -> 60 over the first window and never exceeds the elapsed frames (plotly: frame 0 -> 1 pt, frame 120 -> 63 pts).
findings.actual: frame 0: chemtrail_len= 842 head_len=1; frame 30: 872; frame 58: 900; frame 59: 0; frame 60: 1; frame 120: 61 (2-D run identical: 842/872/900/0/2/61). plotly same call: frame 0 traces [2, 2, 1, 1]; frame 120 [60, 60, 63, 63].
docs_impact: examples/chemtrails.py (gallery gif shows the artifact in its first 2s)

findings.title: animate_plotly.py cannot finish in reasonable time: the spin.gif export renders 900 frames through kaleido (~25-40 min measured/extrapolated; killed at 600s with no output)
findings.description: The example's second call (hyp.plot(data, animate='spin', duration=30, backend='plotly', save_path='spin.gif', show=False)) goes through plotly_backend._export_animation_file, which rasterizes EVERY frame via kaleido/Chromium (snapshot.to_image per frame). duration=30 x frame_rate=30 = 900 frames. Measured this session: a 10-frame export took 28.0s (kaleido 1.3.0 works -- no deadlock -- but ~2-3 s/frame); the verbatim example was killed at a 600s cap with no spin.gif produced (a prior session independently killed it at 420s). Extrapolation: ~25-40 minutes for the verbatim example -- an order of magnitude over the 3-minute example budget. Any user copying the example will believe hypertools hung; every docs build whose md5 changes re-pays this cost (docs/conf.py filename_pattern r'.*\.py' executes it). Mitigations: a much shorter duration/frame_rate for the saved gif in the example (e.g. duration=4, frame_rate=15 -> 60 frames ~ 2-3 min), a progress indicator in _export_animation_file, and/or documenting the per-frame kaleido cost in the example text.

findings.title: save_movie.py silently drops subject 17: data[:17] + data[18:] covers 35 of the 36 weights subjects
findings.description: hyp.load('weights') returns a list of 36 arrays (verified: len=36, each (300, 100)). The example computes group1 = np.mean(data[:17], 0) (subjects 0-16, n=17) and group2 = np.mean(data[18:], 0) (subjects 18-35, n=18): subject index 17 belongs to NEITHER group, and the groups are unequal. Clearly a legacy off-by-one (intended split data[:18] / data[18:]). Runs fine and looks fine, but scientists copy this exact group-averaging pattern.

findings.title: Docstring claim 'Both backends generate exactly frame_rate * duration frames' is off by one for matplotlib animate=True on some input lengths (901 vs plotly's 900 for weights_avg)
findings.description: hyp.plot's frame_rate docstring (plot.py ~line 864) claims exact frame-count parity across backends. For animate=True/'parallel' the matplotlib backend's frame count is the INTERPOLATED data length (x[0].shape[0]), produced by _shared/helpers.py interp_array via np.arange(0, len(arr)-1, 1/interp_val) with interp_val = frame_rate*duration/(n-1). Floating-point fencepost: 300-row weights_avg -> 901 frames (save_movie's exported mp4 ffprobe: nb_frames=901, duration=30.033008), while 200-row synthetic data -> exactly 900. The plotly backend always generates int(round(frame_rate*duration)) = 900. Impact is one extra 33ms frame -- negligible visually -- but the 'exactly' and the cross-backend parity statement do not reproduce, and animation code that assumes frame_rate*duration frames (e.g. per-frame schedules) can be off by one.
findings.repro:
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d300 = hyp.load('weights_avg')
_, ani = hyp.plot(d300, animate=True, show=False)
print('mpl 300-row:', len(list(ani.new_frame_seq())))   # 901
d200 = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(42).standard_normal((200, 8)), axis=0)
_, ani2 = hyp.plot(d200, animate=True, show=False)
print('mpl 200-row:', len(list(ani2.new_frame_seq())))  # 900
figp = hyp.plot(d300, animate=True, backend='plotly', show=False)
print('plotly:', len(figp.frames))                       # 900
findings.expected: Exactly 900 frames on both backends for duration=30, frame_rate=30, per the docstring.
findings.actual: matplotlib: 901 frames for 300-row input (ffprobe of saved mp4: nb_frames=901 duration=30.033008), 900 for 200-row input; plotly: 900 in all cases.

findings.title: animate_surface_morph.py per-frame timing claim ('roughly 20ms/frame instead of ~100ms+, measured on this machine') does not reproduce under either plausible reading
findings.description: Measured this session on the same machine: smooth_hull_3d on a 400-point cloud costs 9.1 ms/call at rounds=2 and 35.5 ms/call at rounds=3 (smoothing-only reading: claim overstates both numbers ~2-3x). The prior 2026-07-11 audit session measured the FULL per-frame draw at ~91 ms (smoothing=2) vs ~370 ms (smoothing=3) (whole-frame reading: claim understates both ~4x). The 4x ratio and the conclusion (2 rounds is much cheaper) hold, but neither reading reproduces '20ms' vs '~100ms+'. Docs-build reality: the example took 01:57.017 in the last executed build (docs/sg_execution_times.rst), i.e. ~325 ms/frame including capture overhead.
findings.repro:
import time, numpy as np
from hypertools.plot.meshutil import smooth_hull_3d
pts = np.random.default_rng(42).standard_normal((400, 3)); pts /= np.abs(pts).max()
for rounds in (2, 3):
    smooth_hull_3d(pts, rounds=rounds)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    for _ in range(10): smooth_hull_3d(pts, rounds=rounds)
    print(rounds, (time.monotonic()-t0)*100, 'ms/call')
findings.expected: ~20 ms/frame at 2 smoothing rounds and ~100 ms+ at 3, per the example docstring.
findings.actual: rounds=2: 9.1 ms per smooth_hull_3d call; rounds=3: 35.5 ms per smooth_hull_3d call (prior session, full _draw_frame: ~91 ms vs ~370 ms).

findings.title: Exported GIFs play ~10% fast at the default frame_rate=30: the 33.33ms delay quantizes to 30ms (GIF centiseconds), so a 30s animation plays in 27s
findings.description: GIF frame delays are stored in centiseconds. Both export paths request 1000/frame_rate ms (matplotlib PillowWriter fps=30; plotly path frame_ms=int(round(1000/30))=33), which Pillow stores as 3 cs = 30 ms. The committed examples/spin.gif demonstrates it: 900 frames x 30 ms = 27.0 s of playback for a duration=30 export. hypertools/plot/animate.py's comment promises 'an exported file plays in real time: ... total ~= duration seconds'; at the DEFAULT frame_rate=30 every gif is 10% fast. frame rates that divide 100 (10, 20, 25, 50) are exact -- verified: the E01 gif at frame_rate=10 stores exactly 100 ms/frame. Consider snapping gif delays to centiseconds (adjusting frame count) or documenting the quantization.
findings.repro: /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "from PIL import Image; im = Image.open('/Users/jmanning/hypertools/examples/spin.gif'); print(im.n_frames, im.info.get('duration'))"
findings.expected: ~33ms effective per-frame delay (900 frames ~= 30s playback), or a documented caveat.
findings.actual: committed spin.gif: frames= 900 size= (640, 480) per-frame ms= 30 (=> 27.0s); E01 gif at 10 fps: dur_ms=100 (exact).

findings.title: save_path failure modes are cryptic: unsupported extension surfaces as a raw ffmpeg CalledProcessError only AFTER rendering all frames; nonexistent directory as a bare FileNotFoundError
findings.description: plot/animate.py dispatches on extension with gif/png/apng/svg special-cased and EVERYTHING ELSE sent to the ffmpeg writer. save_path='out.xyz' therefore renders every animation frame, pipes them to ffmpeg, and dies with subprocess.CalledProcessError exposing the full raw ffmpeg command line; the actionable hint ('use a standard extension') is buried in ffmpeg stderr above the traceback. save_path into a missing directory raises bare FileNotFoundError: '/nonexistent_dir_d06' with no mention of save_path. Validating the extension (naming gif/png/apng/svg/mp4/mov/avi) and the parent directory up front, before rendering, would fail fast with clear messages.
findings.repro:
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((30, 4)), axis=0)
hyp.plot([d, d + 1], animate=True, duration=1, frame_rate=5, save_path='out.xyz', show=False)
findings.expected: Fast ValueError before rendering: "save_path extension '.xyz' is not supported; use .gif/.png/.apng/.svg/.mp4/.mov/.avi" (and similarly a clear error naming save_path for a missing directory).
findings.actual: raised CalledProcessError: Command '['ffmpeg', '-f', 'rawvideo', '-vcodec', 'rawvideo', '-s', '1280x960', '-pix_fmt', 'rgba', '-framerate', '5', ...]' ; MovieWriter stderr: Unable to choose an output format for '...edge_E04.xyz'; use a standard extension for the filename ... / raised FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/nonexistent_dir_d06'

findings.title: animate_MDS.py emits two sklearn FutureWarnings on every run (MDS init/n_init defaults changing in sklearn 1.9/1.10)
findings.description: Running the example verbatim prints: FutureWarning: The default value of `init` will change from 'random' to 'classical_mds' in 1.10 and FutureWarning: The default value of `n_init` will change from 4 to 1 in 1.9. Beyond the noise (gallery pages and every user run), the upstream default changes will silently CHANGE this example's output geometry when sklearn is upgraded. hypertools' MDS wrapper (or the example) should pin init=/n_init= explicitly.
findings.expected: No deprecation warnings from a gallery example; stable output across sklearn upgrades.
findings.actual: FutureWarning: The default value of `init` will change from 'random' to 'classical_mds' in 1.10. To suppress this warning, provide some value of `init`. / FutureWarning: The default value of `n_init` will change from 4 to 1 in 1.9. To suppress this warning, provide some value of `n_init`.

findings.title: chemtrails/precog/bullettime reject a numpy bool array with a cryptic numpy ValueError that names neither the kwarg nor the fix
findings.description: The docstring says 'bool or list of bool'. Passing the library's lingua franca -- a numpy array, e.g. chemtrails=np.array([True, False]) (the natural result of a vectorized condition) -- reaches hypertools/plot/trails.py line 49 broadcast_trail_flag's scalar branch, whose bool(value) raises numpy's 'truth value of an array is ambiguous' ValueError with no mention of chemtrails or of passing a list. Either accept array-likes (list(np.asarray(value).ravel()) when value has __len__) or raise a TypeError naming the kwarg and the accepted types.
findings.repro:
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
t = np.linspace(0, 12.5, 40)
a = np.column_stack([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), t / 4])
b = a + [3, 0, 0]
hyp.plot([a, b], animate=True, chemtrails=np.array([True, False]), duration=1, frame_rate=5, show=False)
findings.expected: Either per-dataset behavior identical to chemtrails=[True, False], or a clear error naming chemtrails and the accepted types (the length-mismatch path already sets that standard: 'chemtrails list has 1 entries but there are 2 datasets...').
findings.actual: File "/Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/trails.py", line 49, in broadcast_trail_flag: return [bool(value)] * n -> ValueError: The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous. Use a.any() or a.all()

findings.title: animate_surface_morph.py's final 'fade the point layer' line is a silent no-op: it sets alpha on a hidden artist, so the visible point texture stays fully opaque
findings.description: The example ends with fig.axes[0].get_lines()[0].set_alpha(0.25) under the comment 'fade the point layer to a subtle texture underneath the hull surface', and the module docstring promises 'the points are kept only as a faint texture underneath the surface (set below)'. But under animate='morph' every per-dataset line is hidden (set_visible(False)) and the visible traveling point cloud is a separate morph artist appended LAST to the axes. Verified line states after the example: [(0, visible=False, alpha=0.25, 1 pt), ..., (5, visible=True, alpha=None, 400 pts)] -- the alpha landed on invisible line 0 while visible line 5 stays fully opaque, rendering as dense black speckles on the hull (see as-is vs intended-fade comparison PNGs at frame 300). Fix: target get_lines()[-1] (or expose the morph artist / honor per-dataset alpha in the morph path).
findings.repro:
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import runpy
g = runpy.run_path('/Users/jmanning/hypertools/examples/animate_surface_morph.py', run_name='__main__')
fig = g['fig']
print([(i, ln.get_visible(), ln.get_alpha(), len(ln.get_xdata())) for i, ln in enumerate(fig.axes[0].get_lines())])
findings.expected: The visible traveling point cloud renders at alpha 0.25 (faint texture under the hull).
findings.actual: lines: [(0, False, 0.25, 1), (1, False, None, 1), (2, False, None, 1), (3, False, None, 1), (4, False, None, 1), (5, True, None, 400)] -- alpha applied to a hidden artist; visible points fully opaque.
docs_impact: examples/animate_surface_morph.py (final line + module docstring 'faint texture' promise)
